title: Rabbi Bisa
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: He was the father of Rabbi Chama and the grandfather of Rabbi Oshaya, the arranger of the baraitot. Rabbi Bisa merited to see his grandson great in Torah, as in [Bava Batra 59a](https://www.sefaria.org/Bava_Batra.59a.5): there was a dispute between Rabbi Oshaya and his father Rabbi Chama about a law; they came and asked Rabbi Bisa, and he ruled like his grandson. Rami bar Chama applied to them: “And a threefold cord is not quickly broken” ([Ecclesiastes 4:12](https://www.sefaria.org/Ecclesiastes.4.12)).
The Ra’avad wrote (cited in the Introduction of the Rambam) that Rabbi Bisa was in the court of our holy Rabbi; Hyman adds that the Rambam too agrees with him.

In [Jerusalem Talmud Gittin 4:4](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Gittin.4.4.7): “The Rabbis of Caesarea say in the name of Rabbi Bisa”; Hyman proposes Rabbi Nasa, as the statement is cited in [Jerusalem Talmud Pesachim 2:2](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Pesachim.2.2.16).[^2]

notes.text: בן בנו is grandson. Hyman’s reported Raavad/Rambam agreement and Nasa emendation remain attributed; Gittin4:4 and Pesachim2:2 are Jerusalem Talmud.

The linked Bavli gives Bisa as Chama’s father and Oshaya’s grandfather, and [Heilprin](https://www.girsology.com/seder-hadorot.html?entry=705&lang=en) quotes the same case. In the two linked Yerushalmi parallels, Gittin has the Rabbis of Caesarea transmitting in Rabbi Bisa’s name, while Pesachim has Rabbi Nasa. Hyman proposes reading Nasa in Gittin.
